evidence.field: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt; U+5142 kMandarin; U+65E1 kMandarin; U+3905 kMandarin
evidence.text: The exact local kMandarin rows give 兂 zān, 旡 jì, and 㤅 yǒng. These are present-day metadata readings, not evidence for an ancient phonetic relationship. The local Baxter–Sagart TSV has no entries for these three characters. Unicode character-record URLs were attempted for all three, but the web tool could not access them, so the local readings have no verified upstream click-through citation in this research.
evidence.title: Unihan_Readings.txt; Unicode Unihan record attempts

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: C04772 旡; pronunciation and Guangyun source listing
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Mandarin jì and cites the historical dictionary readings 居未切 in Shuowen and 居毅切 in Guangyun. This establishes the recorded reading history of 旡 in those dictionary traditions; it does not alone establish its role as phonetic in 㤅.
evidence.title: [C04772] 旡 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: 愛 entry; 形義通解 and 說文/廣韻 sections
evidence.text: The entry attributes the early bronze form 㤅 to 心 plus phonetic 兂, and reports the *Shuowen* analysis of 㤅 as 心 plus 兂声. It separately records 愛 as 从夊、㤅聲, with fanqie 烏代. These are source assertions about graph analysis and dictionary pronunciation, not a matched phonetic reconstruction for 兂 and 㤅.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 愛

evidence.text: This secondary entry analyzes 㤅 as phonetic 旡 plus semantic 心, gives Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *kɯds for 旡, and defers 㤅’s pronunciation to 愛. Its cited account therefore does not give a same-system reconstruction pair for 旡 and 㤅. Separately, CUHK identifies 兂 as the sound element, so the component identification itself is disputed in the inspected sources.
evidence.title: 㤅 — 维基词典

evidence.text: This entry gives Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *qɯːds for 愛 and *kɯds for 旡, and separately gives a Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for 愛. Since it provides no Baxter–Sagart row for 旡 here and the repository’s Baxter–Sagart TSV has neither row, those reconstructions cannot be presented as a verified same-system pair. The 愛 reconstruction is the host’s reading, not an independently verified reconstruction for the proposed component.
evidence.title: 愛 — Wiktionary

search_audit.query: 㤅 兂 旡 pronunciation Old Chinese reconstruction; 兂 旡 㤅 說文 讀音 反切; Unicode Unihan records
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Taiwan MOE 旡 entry and Chinese Wiktionary 㤅 entry. Search results surfaced other dictionary pages; CUHK’s Shuowen-specific result failed to open. Unicode character pages were attempted but inaccessible.

search_audit.query: 㤅 Middle Chinese Guangyun fanqie 愛 㤅 反切; 㤅 上古音 Baxter Sagart; 兂 上古音 Zhengzhang Baxter Sagart
search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the CUHK 愛 entry and Wiktionary 愛 entry. The CUHK account identifies 兂 as phonetic in 㤅 and provides 愛’s fanqie; it does not provide a same-system component-host reconstruction pair. Ctext and CHISE pages appeared in search results but their open attempts failed.

gaps: No official Unicode Unihan character page could be opened for 兂 (U+5142), 旡 (U+65E1), or 㤅 (U+3905). The exact local kMandarin rows were checked, but cannot be emitted as externally verified readings without an accessible official upstream page.
The repository Baxter–Sagart TSV contains no rows for 兂, 旡, or 㤅. Do not manufacture a Baxter–Sagart component-host comparison from a host-only reconstruction.

The sources disagree about whether 兂 or 旡 is the relevant upper component of 㤅. CUHK’s inspected entry says 兂声; Wiktionary’s 㤅 entry represents the form as ⿱旡心 and gives 旡 as phonetic. The historical graph identity and matching pronunciation comparison remain unresolved.
No same-system historical pair was established for 兂/㤅 or 旡/㤅. Keep the sound array empty; neither modern Mandarin readings nor a host-only 爱/愛 reconstruction proves the ancient sound relation.
